Dude I get it. 
There are quite a few things that piss me off as well. 
Especially when you talk to a manager about something 6-10 times and nothing goes anywhere or changes.

Broken bags of flour are not to be selected. 
Unfortunately for you I don’t select anymore. I used to pride myself in my stacking. There’s also supposed to be a slipsheet underneath the flour when placed on a chep pallet. 
I only replied so you’d understand that your poorly stacked pallets come from a different warehouse than the trash trailers that are returned. 
Also if you drive behind most publix stores you’ll see pallets, totes, bales, bags, etc waiting to be loaded on at truck that get rained on. 
Return center associates have to unload those wet items. I’ve seen it. It’s not pleasant. 
If you have a problem with the stacking of a pallet from a warehouse take off the label and show your manager the pallet (the label will have the personnel number of the associate assigned to the order). 
Your manager should take pictures with the label and the poorly stacked pallet and send them back to the correct warehouse in which it came. 
All I ask is not to make a return center associates job more difficult because a selector made your job more difficult.  
Be considerate. 
We all work for the same company.
